artworks.title: The Death of Chione
artworks.description: Poussin stages Artemis' arrow through Chione's tongue — the blasphemy that shatters Daedalion. In Ovid the grieving father races to Parnassus and is changed into a hawk before he can fall; the painting freezes the death that drives that metamorphosis.

artworks.title: Daedalion Transformed into a Hawk
artworks.description: Early twentieth-century plate of Daedalion mid-change: Apollo's pity turns the warrior's leap from Parnassus into the hawk that still hunts other birds — Ovid's aetiology of the raptor's rage.

artworks.title: Diana Killing Chione
artworks.description: Tempesta's Metamorphoses plate (MET): Diana's arrow strikes Chione while her twin sons look on — the crime that sends Daedalion toward the cliff and the hawk.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Book 11: after Artemis kills Chione, Daedalion leaps from Parnassus and Apollo changes him into a hawk — the morning-star's fierce son become bird of prey.

popCulture.title: Daedalion
popCulture.description: Son of Phosphorus and father of Chione — warrior turned hawk in Ovid's Metamorphoses.
